sources.quote: Only HST and licensing may be excluded, and the ad must say so prominently
sources.title: All-in Price Advertising | OMVIC
sources.evidence: The price advertised for a motor vehicle must include all fees and charges the dealer intends to collect, with the exception of HST and licensing. The only exception to the all-in pricing requirements is HST and licensing provided that the advertisement indicates in a clear, comprehensible and prominent manner that those charges are not included.

sources.quote: Only GST and actual financing costs may be added, on every channel
sources.title: All-in advertised pricing - Alberta Motor Vehicle Industry Council
sources.evidence: When an AMVIC-licensed seller advertises the price of a vehicle it must include ALL fees and charges the seller intends to charge. The only fee that can be added to the advertised price is GST and costs associated with financing (if applicable). Automotive Business Regulation Section 11(2)(l).

sources.quote: Vehicle Sales Authority of BC, Motor Dealer Act | All charges other than taxes
sources.publisher: Vehicle Sales Authority of British Columbia
sources.title: Understanding Dealer Fees
sources.evidence: The price you see on the window sticker, as well as any other advertisement, must be the total price, which is the full amount you have to pay to purchase the vehicle (with the exception of taxes). Total price includes all documentation fees, inspection fees, or any other fees and transportation charges.

sources.quote: The all-inclusive price the consumer pays, apart from GST and QST
sources.publisher: Office de la protection du consommateur (Quebec)
sources.title: False Information or Misleading Advertising - Used Automobile Purchased From a Dealer
sources.evidence: Merchants advertising the price of a vehicle are required to advertise an all-inclusive price, which corresponds to the total amount you will need to pay to obtain the vehicle advertised. In addition to the advertised price, you'll have to pay the GST and QST. If any fees are added to the advertised price, that's illegal.

sources.quote: Transport Canada paused the Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles program in January 2025 and it closed that spring
sources.title: Closed: Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles (iZEV)
sources.evidence: The Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles program was officially paused on January 12, 2025, due to the depletion of its funding ahead of the stated March 31, 2025 end date. The program closed on March 31, 2025.

sources.quote: the incentive is applied at the point of sale by an enrolled dealership rather than claimed afterward
sources.title: Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP)
sources.evidence: The Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP) offers point-of-sale incentives for Canadians, Canadian organizations and businesses who buy or lease an eligible electric vehicle. Only enrolled dealerships and authorized sellers can submit incentive applications. The program will run until March 31, 2031, or earlier if funding is used up. Eligible EVs with an odometer with less than 10,000 km qualify as demonstrators.

sources.quote: set at $1,000 for 2026 with a year end deadline
sources.title: Amount of the financial assistance for a used electric vehicle | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: In 2026, you could obtain a $1,000 of Québec government financial assistance when you purchase a used electric vehicle eligible for the Roulez vert program. The program will end on December 31, 2026.

sources.quote: generally within the current model year plus the four prior ones and under 160,000 kilometres
sources.title: CAMVAP - FAQ
sources.evidence: Your vehicle must have traveled not more than 160,000 kilometres at the time of the hearing, and your vehicle must be of the current or 4 previous model years.

sources.quote: the CRTC treats implied consent under Canada's anti-spam legislation as good for two years after a purchase and six months after an enquiry
sources.title: From Canada’s Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) Guidance on Implied Consent | CRTC
sources.evidence: An existing business relationship is established if the recipient has made a purchase or lease of goods, services, land or interest in land within the two-year period immediately before the day on which the message was sent; an inquiry triggers a six-month period during which consent is implied.
